City Council
AGENDA
A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
April 1, 2013
7:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers
24300 Narbonne Avenue
1.
OPENING CEREMONIES
a.
Call Meeting to Order
b.
Flag Salute
c.
Invocation - Councilmember Sanchez
d.
Roll Call
2.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA
3.
CITY MANAGER'S REPORT
4.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. When addressing the Council, please come to the podium and give your name and address for the record. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
6.
CONSENT AGENDA
All items under the Consent Agenda are considered by the Council to be routine and will be enacted by one motion in the form listed below. There may be separate discussions of these items prior to the time the Council votes on the motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Agenda at the request of any Councilmember or staff.
a.
Motion to Waive Further Reading
b.
Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council meeting held on March 18, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report # 6.B. Minutes
c.
Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report #6.C. -Demands
d.
Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report -item #6.D
e.
Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 6.E
f.
Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 6.F
g.
Monthly report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 6.G
h.
February 2013 Treasurer's Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Satff Report- item 6.H
i.
Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 6.I
j.
Adoption of a Resolution authorizing investments in the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and designating City Officials authorized to deposit or withdraw monies. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 6.J
k.
Adoption of an Ordinance amending Lomita Municipal Code Title VIII by adding Chapter 9 (Car Sharing Permits), which would allow the issuance of permits for car sharing programs. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 6.K
l.
Adoption of a Resolution supporting the preservation of municipal tax exempt financing for cities, counties and other governmental entities. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff report- item 6.L
PUBLIC HEARING
7.
DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF AN ORDINANCE PERTAINING TO LOT LINE ADJUSTMENTS. First Reading of an Ordinance amending Lomita Municipal Code, Section 11-1.54.05 eliminating the requirement for a lot line adjustment to be no more than 25 feet from the original parcel line.
Presented by Principal Planner Velasco.
Staff Report- item #7
8.
DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION ACCEPTING THE 2012 ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT ON THE GENERAL PLAN
Presented by Principal Planner Velasco.
Staff Report- item #8
SCHEDULED MATTERS
9.
DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE APPOINTMENT TO PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION - (1) VACANCY
Presented by City Manager Rock
Staff report- item #9
10.
DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF A DESIGN PROPOSAL FOR THE INTERSECTIONS OF 253RD STREET AT WALNUT STREET AND EBONY LANE (LOMITA TRIANGLE)
Presented by Community Services Director McPherron
Staff Report- item #10
11.
DISCUSSION OF APPEAL PROCEDURES FOR PLANNING COMMISSION DECISIONS Discussion and possible direction to staff to prepare an Ordinance amending Municipal Code Section 11-1.70.16. - Appeals and review of planning commission decisions.
Presented by City Attorney Hogin and Assistant City Manager Sugano.
Staff Report- item #11
12.
GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION - NOVEMBER 5, 2013
A.
Approval of Resolution No. 2013-16, calling and giving notice of the Tuesday, November 5, 2013, General Municipal Election,
B.
Approval Resolution No. 2013-17, requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Los Angeles to render specified services relating to the General Municipal Election to be held on November 5, 2013.
C.
Discussion and Consideration of Resolution No. 2013-18, a procedure to resolve tie votes for elected officers at General Municipal Elections.
Presented by Assistant City Clerk Shumway
Staff Report- item #12
ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution in the City Clerk's office at 24300 Narbonne Avenue.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, you should contact the office of the City Clerk at 310 325-7110 (voice) or the California Relay Service. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility to this meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
April 1, 2013

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m. on Monday,
April 1, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager
Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director
McPherron, Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding,
Administrative Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that a new schedule for United States
Coast Guard (USCG) helicopter training flights has been put in place, which is the result of
recent conversations with the Coast Guard Commander regarding the helicopter noise issue.
According to City Manager Rock, the new schedule states that there will be no training flights
on Mondays or on the weekends, and scheduled training flights will take place between 9
a.m. and 11 a.m., Tuesdays through Thursdays. Non-training USCG helicopter flights may
still occur at any time due to rescues, emergencies or disasters. City Manager Rock added
that the new training flight schedule will be posted on the City’s website, and published in the
City’s newsletter.

City Manager Rock clarified information regarding the temporary nine month permit received
by the City for the operation of the Cypress Water Production Facility, and stated that the
information published in the Daily Breeze lacked factual basis. According to City Manager
Rock, the level of methane detected in the water is very low, at a rate of one part per million,
and that tests for methane, which were conducted today, show no trace of methane found in
the air and low levels in the water. He reminded City Council that they had been informed
about methane and Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) levels on numerous occasions in prior open

  Page 1
 meetings.

City Manager Rock asked that Councilmembers refer all water quality issues requests or
complaints to staff so that staff could both track and address issues in a timely manner.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina stated that he had received a copy of the letter from the California
Department of Public Health (CDPH) regarding the temporary nine month permit for the
Cypress Water Production Facility, and that the information contained in the letter is contrary
to the water quality information provided to City Council on March 18, 2013. Councilmember
Traina then cited from the staff report provided for the City Council meeting on December 17,
2012, which stated that “methane remains consistently at low levels and presents no
hazards at these low concentration levels;” meanwhile, the letter from CDPH states that
methane can pose an explosive hazard to City operations and customers. Councilmember
Traina went on to state that when he voted in favor of approving water blending, he was not
informed about the potential hazards of explosions resulting from methane levels, or about
the high TDS levels in the water, which according to CDPH is above the recommended
levels. According to Councilmember Traina, the main goal of the City Council, in this
instance, is to provide quality water to customers, while meeting the water quality ranges of
MWD. Councilmember Traina then asked that City Council consider suspending water
blending and the distribution of such water to customers until CDPH confirms that the City of
Lomita has mitigated the risk of possible methane explosions to zero, and has achieved
acceptable TDS levels. The motion to place the request on a future agenda failed for a lack
of second.

Councilmember Sanchez clarified that the explosive limits for methane are 50,000 parts per
million, and that the City’s methane level is one part per million, which pose no risk for the
City or its residents. According to Councilmember Sanchez, since there is no interchange
between the water and a flame, there is no way an explosion is possible in water heaters.
Councilmember Sanchez stated that both Councilmember Savidan and himself witnessed
the water testing at the Cypress Water Production Facility earlier in the day, and there was
no methane detected.

Councilmember Savidan stated that he was disappointed with the information provided in the
Daily Breeze regarding the nine month permit for the Cypress Water Production Facility, as it
was very inaccurate.

Mayor Estrada agreed with both Councilmembers Sanchez and Savidan regarding their
statements about the Cypress Water Production Facility, and added that the City needs to
continue with the water blending. Mayor Estrada also reported that she attended a meeting
of the Municipal Area Express (MAX), and informed those in attendance that MAX will cease
operations after June 30, 2013, due to funding issues.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, stated that she was concerned that incomplete information
is consistently provided to residents, and added that the last letter mailed to residents
regarding the water blending process is a good example, as it makes no mention of the

  Page 2
 concerns outlined by CDPH. Ms. Houston asked that staff develop an action plan for dealing
with how the identified water quality deficiencies are going to be mitigated.

Esther Daily, Member of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce Board, informed those in
attendance that the Lomita Chamber had participated in two different events organized by
U.S. Congresswoman Maxine Waters, including the Business Expo. Ms. Daily also invited
everyone to the Lomita Chamber's Breakfast on Friday, April 19, 2013, from 7:30 a.m. to 9
a.m., at which California State Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi will be a speaker.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that the City Council continues to ignore the concerns
of the citizens, and complimented Councilmember Traina for trying to be responsive to
residents.

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, stated that she wanted a guarantee that nothing is going to
blow up in the City because of the methane in water, as well as a guarantee that residents
are not in any danger.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, asked that staff monitor the methane levels in the water on a
daily basis, not monthly as recommended by CDPH, in order to prevent a catastrophic event.
Mr. Kivett also asked whether the City’s insurance would cover the expenses of a
catastrophic event resulting from methane in the water.

Anthony Arevalo, Lomita resident, indicated that it is City Council’s responsibility to act when
their attention is called to an issue. Mr. Arevalo went on to state that since City Council does
not take this issue seriously, he would file complaints with other state agencies and request
that an investigation be conducted regarding the methane and high TDS levels.

Kathy Chew, Lomita resident, stated that she voiced her concerns for some time at City
Council meetings, but City Council continues to ignore the concerns of residents. Ms. Chew
also put the City on notice, stating that if anything happens as a result of the issues related
to methane or TDS, she would seek legal actions against the City.

Lawson Pedigo, Lomita resident, stated that he was concerned with the quality of
groundwater from the aquifers, which in turn could result in poor water quality.

Bob Knight, Lomita resident, stated that he was also concerned with the methane and TDS
levels, and asked that City Council bring back the consultants in order to solve the issues.

Kent Edmonds, Lomita resident, stated that he was concerned that the water blending could
cause damage to pipes and household appliances, as it happened before in 2010. Mr.
Edmonds also added that such water quality issues could affect property values.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, stated that the issues concerning water quality are directly
related to the well. Mr. Albert recommended that constant monitoring be conducted at the
water tank to ensure that methane levels remain low, so the water does not become the
vessel for transporting methane. Mr. Albert also suggested capping the well, and using it
only for emergency purposes. Finally, Mr. Albert stated that it is the obligation of the City
Council to provide good quality water to residents.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that he was concerned that the City Attorney was

  Page 3
 texting during the meeting.

City Manager Rock reiterated that the amount of methane in the water is between zero to
one part per million, that no methane had been detected in the air, and that the explosive
level for methane is 50,000 parts per million. City Manager Rock went on to add that
methane is not a regulated constituent of Title 22, but the City will monitor methane levels
and do everything asked by CDPH. According to City Manager Rock, the safe drinking water
standards have been met, and that the water taste tests were legitimate.

Claude Hill, Lomita resident, stated that according to his son, who is a scientist, the water
could taste great and not be dangerous to drink, but under certain circumstances the water
could be explosive because of the methane.

In response to Councilmember Gazeley’s question regarding how often water testing will be
conducted to monitor methane levels, Public Works Director Damasse stated that CDPH
requires that testing be performed weekly, but staff will perform the tests daily.

6. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Gazeley
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

a. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council meeting held on
  March 18, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

b. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

c. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

d. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

e. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

f. Monthly report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

g. February 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

h. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

i. Adoption of a Resolution authorizing investments in the Local Agency Investment Fund
  (LAIF) and designating City Officials authorized to deposit or withdraw monies.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

j. Adoption of an Ordinance amending the Lomita Municipal Code, Title VIII, by adding
  Chapter 9 (Car Sharing Permits), which would allow the issuance of permits for car sharing
  programs. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  Page 4
 k. Adoption of a Resolution supporting the preservation of municipal tax exempt financing for
  cities, counties, and other governmental entities. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARING

7. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF AN ORDINANCE PERTAINING TO LOT LINE
  ADJUSTMENTS

 Councilmember Sanchez moved to continue this item to the next scheduled City Council
 meeting in order for Council to have additional time to review the item. Councilmember
 Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

8. DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION ACCEPTING THE 2012
  ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT ON THE GENERAL PLAN

Principal Planner Velasco stated that Government Code Section 65400 requires planning
agencies to provide an annual report to their legislative bodies regarding the status and
implementation of their general plans; the reporting period for the City of Lomita’s Annual
Progress Report is from January 1, 2012, to December 31, 2012. According to Principal
Planner Velasco, there were no revisions to the General Plan in 2012, and that only the
Housing Element is required to be updated and approved by the State of California.
Principal Planner Velasco then provided an overview and listing of the housing programs in
the City, as well as new development in 2012.

George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, stated that he was a
member of the General Plan Advisory Committee in 1998, and that back then the Committee
conducted only a very limited review of downtown commercial areas, and touching just
briefly on traffic-related issues. Mr. Kivett recommended that a full review of the General
Plan be initiated, as many changes have taken place since 1998. As for the Housing
Element, Mr. Kivett suggested keeping the density at the same levels.

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve item #8, with the one change pointed out by
Principal Planner Velasco, and adding Lomita Manor under low income housing
preservation. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

9. DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE APPOINTMENT TO PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  - (1) VACANCY

Councilmembers Gazeley, Savidan, and Sanchez nominated Ken Blackwood for the Parks
and Recreation Commission.

Ken Blackwood was appointed to the Parks and Recreation Commission.

10. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF A DESIGN PROPOSAL FOR THE INTERSECTIONS
  OF 253RD STREET AT WALNUT STREET AND EBONY LANE (LOMITA TRIANGLE)

Community Services Director McPherron stated that Public Safety and Traffic Commission
had reviewed previous designs, along with two new designs, for the Lomita Triangle, and

  Page 5
 recommended three of those designs for further discussion and City Council consideration.
Director McPherron went on to provide an overview of recommended designs, and stated
that the total cost, including engineering, design, and general construction, had been
estimated at $120,000. Since the Community Services Department does not have sufficient
funds to complete the redesign of the Lomita Triangle, Director McPherron suggested
including Alternative D in the upcoming budget discussion for the Capital Improvement Plan
for Fiscal Year 2013-2014.

Discussion followed on whether the area at the stop sign, westbound of 253rd street, would
have enough space to accommodate traffic during busy hours; to that discussion Irene
Guilmette, Los Angeles County Traffic Engineer, stated that it could be a concern during
school hours, however, she did not foresee that much of a problem. In response to
Councilmember’s Traina’s question whether a “keep clear” marking could be installed if
needed, Ms. Guilmette responded positively that such a marking could be installed.

Discussion followed about the best alternative for the intersection and whether a public
hearing was needed for this item, as it affects residents in that area. Councilmember
Gazeley expressed his concern that allowing through-traffic might affect residents at that
intersection. Director McPherron indicated that the results of a survey mailed out about year
ago to 197 residents in the area, asking whether they were in favor of removing the right turn
at the Lomita Triangle, showed the majority of responses were in favor of removing the right
turn, with 47 responses in favor, and 19 responses not in favor. However, according to
Director McPherron, the survey did not include questions regarding through traffic.

Planning Commissioner Jones informed City Council that public hearings were scheduled at
the Public Safety and Traffic Commission, and added that there is already a problem at the
intersection, as it is not ADA complaint. Mr. Jones also stated that he had talked to some
residents in the area that were interested in making the intersection permit through-traffic.

Mayor Estrada moved to place the Lomita Triangle project on the City’s Capital Improvement
Plan for 2013-2014, which will be discussed during the upcoming budget hearing. The
motion died for the lack of second.

Councilmember Traina made a motion to have a public hearing on the Lomita Triangle, and
to notify the residents in the area. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which
carried unanimously.

11. DISCUSSION OF APPEAL PROCEDURES FOR PLANNING COMMISSION DECISIONS

City Attorney Hogin stated that City Council has eight options when considering appeal
procedures for Planning Commission decision. Councilmember Sanchez moved to go with
Option #2, but to increase the appeal process from 15 to 21 calendar days, as indicated in
Option #8. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion. City Attorney Hogin clarified that
this decision would require staff to bring forward an ordinance amending the Municipal Code,
by changing the Planning Commission’s role from a decision-making body, to that of an
Advisory Board, which would also mean that any application (ZMA, CUP, etc.) would have to
be agendized for approval by the City Council. Councilmember Savidan added that that
particular option would mean that the City Council would have to review and approve every
Planning Commission decision. Discussion followed on whether City Council would like to
review and approve all Planning Commission items.

  Page 6
 Mayor Estrada made a substitute motion to maintain the status quo regarding the appeal
procedures for Planning Commissions decisions. The motion died for the lack of second.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, was called to speak, as he had submitted a speaker card,
but he had left the City Council Chambers.

Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, and Gazeley agreed that Council needed more time to
review the available options regarding the appeal procedures for Planning Commissions
decisions. Councilmember Gazeley amended his second on the previous motion, and
moved to table this item. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

12. GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION – NOVEMBER 5, 2013

Assistant City Clerk Shumway stated that in compliance with the California Elections Code,
the City Council needs to approve a Resolution calling for, and giving notice of, an election,
as well as a Resolution requesting specified services from Los Angeles County relating to
the conduct of the General Municipal Election. According to Assistant City Clerk Shumway,
Resolution No. 2007-39, established requirements for candidate statements; however, the
City Council has the option to increase the permissible length of candidate statements, from
200 to 400 words, and could also decide if the City, or the candidate, would pay (currently
$175) for the translation of candidate statements into Spanish. Assistant City Clerk
Shumway also stated that if the General Municipal Election results in a tie vote, then there
are two options for reconciling the tie, by lot or by conducting a Special Runoff Election; the
estimated cost of a Special Runoff Election is currently$40,000.

Mayor Estrada stated that she was not in favor of resolving a tie vote by lot. Mayor Estrada
moved to adopt Resolutions Calling For and Giving Notice Of the November 5, 2013,
General Municipal Election, and requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Los
Angeles to render specified services relating to the General Municipal Election, as well as
limiting candidate statements to no more than 200 words, for which the City will cover the
cost of translation services, and finally having a Special Runoff Election in the case of a tie
vote. Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:59 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC

  Page 7
